paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.
model_annotation: The line chart displays the performance of two methods—“ST-ES” and “Random”—in terms of minADE₂₀ (a trajectory prediction error metric) as a function of the number of in-context examples, ranging from 0 to 8. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” is linearly scaled with integer tick marks at 0, 2, 4, 6, and 8. The y-axis, labeled “minADE₂₀ (←),” is linearly scaled and spans approximately 0.128 to 0.142, with major tick marks labeled at 0.13, 0.135, 0.14, and 0.145. The “ST-ES” method is represented by a blue line with circular markers and a solid line style; it begins at approximately 0.141 at 0 examples, drops sharply to 0.132 at 1 example, fluctuates slightly between 0.130 and 0.132 from 2 to 5 examples, then rises modestly to 0.132 at 6, peaks at 0.133 at 7, and ends at 0.132 at 8 examples. The “Random” method is shown as an orange line with circular markers and a solid line style; it starts at 0.142 at 0 examples, drops to 0.131 at 1, remains nearly flat at 0.131 through 3 examples, rises to 0.132 at 4, peaks at 0.135 at 5, dips to 0.130 at 6, then climbs to 0.134 at 7 and ends at 0.136 at 8 examples.
